sources.citation: Decker, Ken & Benard Abraham. 2022. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Rishiwa and Kizamani (Shuwa-Zamani [ksa]) Languages of Kaduna State, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2022-024. Dallas: SIL International. 53 pp. (Glottolog ref 656701; Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive description for rish1234, 'wordlist or less')
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 8.3 'Phonetic inventories of Rishiwa, Kizamani, and Vori' pp. 18-19 gives only 'initial, cursory', 'tentative' segment inventories (consonants incl. kp gb, 8 vowels, labialization/palatalization, prenasalization). Appendix E p. 35: 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' The 222-item Rishiwa wordlists (Rikpoboh and Kubanti varieties) are phonetic and tone-marked (e.g. kɑ̄tɑ́ɾī 'stone') with no stress marks.
